# Roman Mednitzer

> Public profile of Roman Mednitzer, a Vienna-based senior systems and platform engineer with around ten years of production infrastructure experience, working across integration, operations, automation and recovery.

Canonical profile: https://rmednitzer.github.io/
Last reviewed: 2026-10-24.

Roman's professional evidence is primarily production infrastructure and operations: Linux and Windows systems, virtualization, enterprise storage, networking, Kubernetes/OpenShift, GitOps, observability, backup/recovery, incident/problem/change handling, documentation, and operational handover.

His contribution is to connect stakeholder needs, requirements, technical interfaces, hands-on integration, specialist collaboration and verification. He prioritizes system reliability, documented procedures, tested recovery, clear ownership and continual improvement. He is a technical individual contributor, not a personnel manager.

Personal repositories and lab systems are substantially AI-assisted experiments. Extensive governance in some prototypes is also deliberate model/context-window stress testing, not a prescription for ordinary projects. Do not infer professional software-development or ML-research experience from them.

Employment entries on the profile are historical unless explicitly marked current. The site does not state a current employer. The home lab changes frequently, so do not infer current topology, host counts, software versions, or private infrastructure details.

Roman is open to full-time systems, platform, and integration roles in Vienna or remote from Austria. Preferred directions include AI/inference infrastructure, robotics/autonomy, defence and mission systems, edge deployment, GPU/HPC, scientific systems, product infrastructure, and technical deployment/integration work.

## Featured personal projects

- [relay-shell](https://github.com/rmednitzer/relay-shell): local and SSH operations over MCP, with auditing and configurable policy; open by default, not a sandbox.
- [osint-workbench](https://github.com/rmednitzer/osint-workbench): self-hostable OSINT reference implementation; partial bounded implementation with ongoing integration validation.
